title: Oncall rotation deconflict and duty-concierge procedures
author: Sofia Tran
body:
Summary
-------
This doc defines the deconfliction process for overlapping on-call assignments, the Duty Concierge role (a short-lived coordination persona), and standardized procedures for quiet windows, after-hours escalation, and runbook handoffs. It is intended for SRE/Platform/Serving teams who operate Redwood inference endpoints and for engineering managers who approve rotations.

Why this exists
----------------
As Redwood scales with more services (serve-runtime, request-router, kv-cache, console-api), we see two recurring failures: (1) duplicate pagers causing fractured ownership during handoffs, and (2) poorly coordinated quiet windows that delay mitigation. The Duty Concierge pattern reduces cognitive load on responders and keeps customer communication and exec escalation consistent.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all 24/7 responder rotations for production inference endpoints and critical control plane services.
- Does NOT replace escalation matrices for business continuity events (legal/compliance-led incidents).
- Includes guidance for game-day simulations and postmortem evidence collection.

Key roles and responsibilities
-------------------------------
- Primary Oncall (Responder): owns initial triage, containment, and assigning remediation tasks.
- Secondary Oncall (Backup): takes over if Primary is unavailable or incident escalates beyond scope.
- Duty Concierge (Coord): 2–6 hour coordination role during busy handoffs and major incidents. Responsibilities:
  - Deconflict overlapping pages across services.
  - Orchestrate status page and customer comm updates.
  - Temporarily own cross-service ticketing (create single incident ticket and tag owners).
  - Escalate to Incident Commander if impact > P1 threshold.
- Incident Commander (IC): formal incident lead for P1s; not every Duty Concierge is an IC.

Rotation deconflict policy
--------------------------
1. Single active pager rule: only one person should actively page per incident type for a given tenant/region. If multiple pages fire, the first acknowledged responder becomes Primary. Secondary responders should acknowledge with status only ("standing by").
2. Overlap window: when a new rotation starts, outgoing and incoming oncall overlap for 30 minutes (standard) unless manager approves shorter window. During overlap the Duty Concierge should be appointed for at least the first handoff.
3. Emergency takeover: if two primaries claim ownership simultaneously, the Duty Concierge (if present) will mediate. If no Duty Concierge, the first ACK timestamp wins; create an incident ticket and designate an IC within 15 minutes.

Duty Concierge procedure (step-by-step)
---------------------------------------
1. During a planned handoff or after a major event, create a single incident ticket in Jira: project INF-INC; include all paged services and initial evidence (grafana links, paging logs, error traces).
2. Post a short note to #ops-bridge Slack channel: include ticket link, list of affected services, current severity, and suggested owner. Use the template: "[DutyConcierge] Incident INF-INC-<num>: <short summary> — Primary: @username — Status: triage".
3. If customer-facing, prepare a status page draft (see templates below) and hold for Primary ACK. Duty Concierge publishes only after Primary confirms content.
4. Maintain a one-line running log in the Jira ticket with timestamps for each major action (containment, rollback, scale event) until IC declared.
5. At end of coordination window (default 4 hours), hand over the ticket to Primary for ongoing remediation or to the IC for full incident management. Include a short handoff checklist.

Quiet window (after-hours) rules
--------------------------------
- Definition: a quiet window is a pre-declared minimal-notification period during which only high-severity incidents (P1) will generate external customer notices. Quiet windows are used for maintenance and holiday shifts.
- Quiet window thresholds: only alerts that meet P1 criteria (impacting >5% of tenants OR error rates causing >25% p99 latency regression) generate immediate external comms. Everything else is acknowledged in-team and elevated after 30 min if unresolved.
- Process:
  1. Before entering a quiet window, Duty Concierge (or oncall lead) must tag scheduled maintenance in Status Page with planned start/end and risk level.
  2. Configure alert routing: non-P1 alerts route to a low-noise channel and an email digest to rotation lead.
  3. During quiet window, oncall must confirm receipt for any paging event within 5 minutes; if no ACK, escalate to Secondary.

Runbook: KV cache eviction storm (example)
----------------------------------------
Purpose: common cause of sudden p95 latency spikes on serve-runtime when upstream clients trigger mass key invalidations.
Symptoms:
- Rapid increase in cache eviction rate (>1000 evictions/min per pool)
- p95 token latency > 2x baseline and increase in serve-runtime 5xx errors
- "OOM eviction" or "KV checksum mismatch" in serve-runtime logs
First responders:
1. Acknowledge page and set incident severity: if client-facing impact >3 tenants, set P1; otherwise P2.
2. Capture evidence:
   - Grafana dashboard: Runtime -> kv-cache -> eviction-rate (time range last 30m)
   - Logs: kubectl logs --selector app=serve-runtime -n prod --tail=200 | grep "evict"
   - PagerDuty: copy alert payload to Jira ticket.
3. Containment steps (ordered):
   a. Use console-api to temporarily raise per-tenant cache TTLs: POST /api/admin/cache-config {"tenant":"<id>", "ttl_s": 7200} (requires admin role).
   b. If TTL change not possible, scale serve-runtime pool by +20% using autoscaler override: kubectl patch hpa/serve-runtime-hpa -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":<new>}}'.
   c. If errors persist, rollback latest config change to serve-runtime (git tag release) and restart pod set.
4. Long-term remediation: enable detailed tracing for affected tenant, run workload replay in staging, file a change request to add rate-limits on client invalidation API.
5. Post-incident: collect heap profiles, eviction histograms, and store in S3 under s3://incidents/<ticket>/evidence.

Postmortem and evidence checklist
----------------------------------
- Postmortem owner assigned within 72 hours.
- Evidence required in ticket before postmortem draft:
  - Time-series graphs (p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, eviction rate).
  - Relevant logs with ORCID (at least 2 correlated traces).
  - Config changes list (git commits) in 48 hours window.
  - PagerDuty activity log (ACKs, escalations).
  - Customer impact summary (tenants affected, estimated % requests lost).
- Postmortem template (use as headings in Confluence):
  - Summary and impact
  - Timeline (minute-level for first 2 hours)
  - Root cause analysis
  - Contributing factors
  - Remediation and owner(s)
  - Detection and mitigation improvements
  - Follow-up action items with due dates and owners

Game day and simulation checklist (30–90 minute drill)
------------------------------------------------------
- Objective: validate Duty Concierge handoff, status page publishing, and triage within SLO.
- Pre-reqs (2 days before): select scenario (e.g., multi-region capacity failover), nominate ICs, create a synthetic ticket.
- During drill:
  1. Trigger simulated alert (use chaos-monkey lab).
  2. Duty Concierge creates the incident ticket and posts to #ops-bridge.
  3. Primary must ACK in <5 minutes; if not, Secondary takes over.
  4. Duty Concierge drafts and publishes status page update within 20 minutes of the incident start.
  5. Runbook steps exercised and evidence uploaded.
- After drill: 1-hour retro with action items captured in the ticket.

Status page and customer comm templates
--------------------------------------
- Internal short status (Ops Bridge):
  [INF-INC-<num>] <short summary> — Impact: <service(s)> — Status: TRIAGE — Owner: @<user> — ETA: <hh:mm UTC>

- External status template (public):
  Title: Service disruption affecting <service> in <region>
  Body: We are investigating an issue impacting <description of functional impact>. Our engineers are actively triaging; we'll update this page every 30 minutes or as new info becomes available. Affected customers: <list/tenants>. Next update: <hh:mm UTC>.

- Executive briefing (email/Slack to execs):
  Subject: [Action Required] P1: <short summary> — INF-INC-<num>
  Body: One-line impact, estimated customer count, mitigation in progress, immediate customer-facing message, and expected ETA. Include link to Jira ticket and status page.

Escalation thresholds (summary table)
-------------------------------------
| Severity | Customer impact threshold | SLA action | Notify |
| P1 | Any production endpoint down for >5% tenants OR full-region outage | Exec briefing within 30m, legal + sales notified | Pager to IC + execs |
| P2 | Significant degradation (p95 latency >x2 baseline or >25% error spike) | Status page update within 60m | Pager to Primary + Secondary |
| P3 | Minor degradation or single-tenant issue | Internal ticket only, periodic email digest | Ticket assignment |

Appendix: quick commands and dashboard queries
------------------------------------------------
- Grafana: runtime.kv-cache.eviction_rate > 1000 for last 5m
- kubectl: kubectl rollout undo deploy/serve-runtime -n prod --to-revision=<rev>
- cURL status update draft: curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API_TOKEN" -d '{"title":"...","body":"..."}' https://status.redwood.ai/api/v1/incidents

Document governance
--------------------
- Owners: Eng-SRE oncall program (primary), Serve Runtime team (secondary).
- Review cadence: annually or after any P1 with customer impact.
- Training: incorporate Duty Concierge role into new-joiner oncall bootcamp and include a simulated rotation handoff in the first 30 days.

Related pages and references
---------------------------
- Incident operator handbook (link internal)
- PagerDuty integration spec (link internal)
- Postmortem template (link internal)

Contact
-------
For questions about this procedure or to request a rotation exception, contact oncall-program@redwood.ai or @sofia.tran on Slack.
